dates.title: Mizzou Admissions - Dates & Deadlines (incoming freshmen, fall 2027)

apply.title: Mizzou Admissions - How to Apply: International Students

test_policy.notes: Fall 2027 freshman applicants can choose a test-optional review (holistic committee review; short essay and activities list required for the domestic test-optional route). For international applicants, SAT/ACT scores are not required for admission but are preferred for international freshman scholarships; the international pages do not require an essay or resume. Homeschooled students and students from non-accredited schools must submit a score (domestic test-optional page).

requirements.supplemental_essays: None required for international applicants (FAQ: no essay, recommendations, extracurricular summary or interview beyond the listed application materials).
requirements.notes: Mizzou accepts the Mizzou Application or the Common App, with no preference. International fee is $65 (domestic freshmen pay $55); the FAQ offers application fee waivers to first-time freshman applicants within one year of high school graduation who submit an approved ACT, SAT or NACAC waiver form (the fee waiver flag here is left false because the international pages do not mention waivers). Required: online application and fee, transcripts from every school attended (unofficial uploads accepted for review; official final transcript after admission; original-language transcripts plus English translation), and English proficiency. Academic rule: 13 core units (4 math, 3 science, 3 social studies, 2 language, 1 fine arts) with core GPA of at least 2.5 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. Letters of recommendation are not required but are accepted as supplemental material. After admission: proof of financial support for one year, passport copy; all non-native speakers take the ELSP placement exam (by July 15 for fall). Some schools (education, journalism, nursing) set higher English scores than the university minimum.

deadlines.label: Deadline to apply and submit all materials for international freshman scholarships (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: International scholarships page (award table headed Academic Year 2027-28): 'Fall applicants must apply and submit all required application materials by December 1 to be considered for scholarships. Scholarship offers for the fall term will be sent by late January.' It also says 'The deadline to apply for general and departmental scholarships is December 1', and the Dates & Deadlines page lists 'Deadline to apply for admission for priority scholarship consideration - December 1' and 'Deadline to apply for general, competitive and departmental scholarships - December 1'. The Dates & Deadlines page prints no year in its freshman table, but its transfer table on the same page gives explicit Fall 2027 dates (application opens August 1, 2026; FAFSA deadline February 1, 2027), so the page is the 2026-27 cycle. CONFLICT: the international FAQ says 'March 1 for International Admissions scholarships' and 'You must apply and be admitted by March 1 to be automatically considered for scholarship review'; the two current pages above both say December 1 (and promise offers by late January, which a March 1 cutoff would not allow), so Dec 1, 2026 is stored and the FAQ's March 1 looks out of date. Confirm with International Admissions (inter@missouri.edu) if unsure.

deadlines.label: Application deadline, fall 2027 (rolling decisions from October 1)
deadlines.notes: Dates page: application opens August 1, admission decisions released from October 1 and rolling after; fall application deadline July 1. The Dates & Deadlines page prints no year in its freshman table, but its transfer table on the same page gives explicit Fall 2027 dates (application opens August 1, 2026; FAFSA deadline February 1, 2027), so the page is the 2026-27 cycle. The international how-to-apply page says there are no application deadlines and recommends applying 6-12 months before the start of the semester, while the international FAQ gives July 1 for the fall semester. No early action or early decision.

deadlines.label: Honors College application deadline (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Honors College application opens Sept. 15; Honors scholarship deadline Dec. 1; application deadline Feb. 1. Students need not be admitted to Mizzou before applying, but test scores and transcripts must be on file. The Dates & Deadlines page prints no year in its freshman table, but its transfer table on the same page gives explicit Fall 2027 dates (application opens August 1, 2026; FAFSA deadline February 1, 2027), so the page is the 2026-27 cycle.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Proof of English proficiency is required through an approved test, an IGCSE English First Language grade of B or higher, or an IB English A: Language & Literature SL/HL score of 5 or higher. Applicants educated in listed English-speaking countries (for example US, UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada except Quebec, Singapore, South Africa, Nigeria/Ghana/Cameroon/Liberia/Sierra Leone/Gambia with English C or higher on WASSCE or GCE) may not need a score. TOEFL Essentials and IELTS Online are not accepted. Applicants who are ready academically but below the minimum may enter the Academic Integration @ Mizzou (AIM) program. All non-native speakers take the ELSP placement exam before arrival.

english.notes: Old 0-120 scale; the page applies 79 with no section below 17 to tests taken before Jan 26, 2026 (the page also says the new scale started Jan 21, 2026). Higher in some colleges: Education and Journalism 100, Nursing 84 (speaking 26).
New 1-6 scale: minimum 4.5 with no section below 4.0 (Education and Journalism 5.0; Nursing needs 5.0 in speaking).
Academic IELTS only. Education and Journalism 7.0; Nursing 7.0 with 8 in speaking.
Education and Journalism 130; Nursing 115 (115 in production speaking).
C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency; Education, Journalism and Nursing 190.

aid.notes: FAQ: 'Mizzou does not offer need-based financial aid for international students'; the CSS Profile and other need-based forms are neither required nor accepted. All admitted degree-seeking on-campus international freshmen are considered for merit awards, which apply only to the nonresident portion of tuition and generally cannot be combined: International Honors Scholarship $20,000 per year, International Merit Scholarship $10,000 per year (academic year 2027-28), SAT/ACT preferred. Global Black & Gold awards ($21,500 with 1260 SAT/27 ACT; $11,000 with 1200 SAT/25 ACT) require a parent who graduated from Mizzou. Honors College awards (ASH Scholars, Discovery Fellows, Cherng Scholars) need the Honors application; international applicants outside the US are not eligible for the Stamps Scholarship because of its in-person interview.

sat.note: The page prints the College Board (SAT) code as 006875, i.e. 6875 without the leading zeros.

tier_notes.general: AAU public flagship with a 78% overall admit rate (IPEDS fall 2024) and SAT middle 50% of about 1150-1330 on the 10% who sent scores; placed with Iowa, Kentucky and Arkansas.
